description: QuantumCoders is a team of passionate innovators and developers driven by creativity, technology and scientific exploration. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge we aim to develop an innovative health monitoring solution to help astronauts track their health, detect potential risks and maintain their physical and mental well being during long duration space missions. We believe in pushing boundaries and coding solutions that make a difference on Earth and beyond.
summary: QuantumCoders is an intelligent astronaut health monitoring and telemetry hub designed for long duration space missions and microgravity environments. The platform tracks real time physiological indicators including heart rate, blood pressure, core body temperature and sleep duration by combining simulated live telemetry with open source research data from the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR). It features an automated Anomaly Detection Engine that continuously evaluates cardiovascular load, flags risk levels (Nominal, Caution, Elevated) to protect crew safety and allows flight surgeons to generate secure, one click mission reports instantly.
details:
QuantumCoders acts as a centralized command and telemetry dashboard for space missions. It ingests and analyzes time series physiological data streams to monitor astronaut well being. The system includes an automated Anomaly Detection Engine that compares incoming metrics against statistical baselines to detect elevated cardiovascular load or sudden heart rate variance triggering instant warnings and recommendations.

Benefits & Intended Impact: The platform enhances crew safety during extended orbital or interplanetary missions by automating early detection of health degradation. Beyond space exploration it holds massive potential for terrestrial spin offs, such as remote patient monitoring, telemedicine in isolated regions and healthcare tracking in extreme environments.

Tools, Coding Languages, Frameworks & Software:

  • Frontend: Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS hosted on Vercel.
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI deployed on Render.
  • Database & Storage: Supabase
  • Data Sources: Simulated live streams and NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) research datasets.
